headline: Congress cancels the federal approval that let California enforce its Advanced Clean Cars II rules for new cars and trucks.
what_it_does: Under the Clean Air Act, states generally cannot set their own vehicle pollution rules, but California can ask the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for a waiver. EPA had granted California a waiver for its Advanced Clean Cars II rules, which set new requirements for low-emission and zero-emission vehicles. This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel that EPA decision, so the waiver no longer has legal effect. Under that act, EPA also cannot issue a substantially similar waiver unless Congress later allows it.

who_it_affects.group: California state government and the California Air Resources Board
who_it_affects.how: The state loses the federal waiver it needed to enforce its Advanced Clean Cars II vehicle emission rules.
They are no longer required to meet California's Advanced Clean Cars II low-emission and zero-emission vehicle requirements under this waiver.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy new cars in California
who_it_affects.how: The mix of new vehicles offered for sale will not be governed by the Advanced Clean Cars II requirements that the waiver had allowed.

who_it_affects.group: Other states that follow California's vehicle standards
who_it_affects.how: States that chose to adopt California's Advanced Clean Cars II rules may no longer be able to enforce them, since those rules relied on California's waiver.

when_it_takes_effect: June 12, 2025, when the resolution was signed into law.
